title: Ember and Hollow
premise: Mara Villalobos, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent years hiding among the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, trading in memories and small miracles while pretending their blade-oath died with the old covenant. When the border wards collapse and the stars go out on the same night, Mara learns that a guild rival has been harvesting oath-magic to crown himself as the thirteenth moon, and only a reforged covenant between the mortal realm and the Hollow can undo it. Mara must reclaim the swordspeech they buried, gather the scattered witnesses of the original pact, and confront the rival in the Hollow itself. In the end, Mara breaks their own oath to forge a new one—sacrificing their stored memories of who they were before—to relight the stars and bind both realms into an honest, imperfect accord.
about_author: Odile Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three libraries that no longer exist. They write fantasy from a house built on the foundation of a demolished customs office, where they keep meticulous records of things that never happened.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. During a routine ledger audit of impossible trades, the border wards shatter and every star vanishes at once, leaving the guild's contraband miracles flickering and unstable. A dying courier delivers a fragment of the old covenant bearing Mara's own oath-mark. The emotional beat is dread curdling into reluctant recognition: invisibility was always an illusion.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Broken Pact
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with interludes from the guild's memory-broker, Sef. Following the covenant fragment, Mara uncovers that guildmaster Corvane has been buying oaths wholesale, hollowing out their speakers to fuel his ascension as the thirteenth moon. Sef betrays the guild's location of the first witness. The beat is rising resolve shadowed by grief for complicity.

chapters.title: What the Hollow Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara and Corvane POVs. Mara crosses into the Hollow with two witnesses and reforges the first clause of the covenant, but each spoken line costs a memory of their former self. Corvane, half-transfigured and increasingly paranoid, offers Mara restoration in exchange for betrayal. The climax: Mara refuses and duels him in swordspeech beneath the unborn moon.

chapters.title: A Covenant of Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Victorious but nearly emptied, Mara speaks the final clause—surrendering every remaining memory of who they were before the oath—and the stars reignite one by one as the moon completes its thirteenth turn. The realms bind into a new, honest accord; Sef helps Mara begin a fresh ledger. The beat is bittersweet renewal: identity rebuilt from choice, not inheritance.
